# Cohort 128: complete shared observability fixture construction

The shared two-backend harness now returns ONLY the existing observability store.
All three public proof consumers lose raw DB/dialect callbacks; native constructors
at the original opening point own schema/payload setup and reverse close lifetime.
The previous standalone diagnostic cohort uses the original named log writer.

The sole remaining raw consumer was a deliberately contradictory PLATFORM receipt
control, not executable agent/node outcome persistence or compatibility behavior.
Move exactly its three original tuples into a named bounded fault below the
pipeline receipt owner. The closed variant selects only pending/dead-letter,
failed/success or failed/dead-letter counterevidence. No caller-selected SQL,
subscriber, payload, outcome, failure, table or transaction is exposed.

Preserve all original event identity, platform subtype, effects/failure bytes and
processed clock. A private fixed-row native read proves each tuple and exact clock;
the original transaction probe proves one write commit and no active lease. Named
faults validate native owner, canonical event ID, finite variant and nonzero time;
invalid/raw/nil/cancelled/closed attempts refuse. Real public API/read tests retain
all statuses, receipt-versus-delivery precedence, detail failure, payload identity
non-promotion, typed paired filters, grouping, subsecond order and corruption.

Finite whole-source rewrites compare unchanged workloads, exact INSERT columns and
dialect casts, every fixed contradictory value, and all three consumer signatures.
The two existing diagnostic caller recipes are extended, not duplicated. New raw
operations remain private exact-coordinator fixture faults/validation reads and
are individually dispositioned, without guard exceptions or SQL allowances.

This eliminates the raw construction/forwarding seam for the complete shared
observability family. The wider raw run-scoped diagnostic/fork fixture recipes
and parent zero-debt/global completion obligations remain open. No production
runtime/spec change, restoration framework or measured flake reduction is claimed.
